title: Offer repository.publish_resolve for an UNKNOWN publish, and give the Publish card its resolve control
description:
CHILD of task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8 (the operator exit for an UNKNOWN publish), filed by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18. Delivers the operator-facing half of that row's DoD 2. task-21be6e90 is the integration parent and declares dependsOn on this row.

WHY A SEPARATE ROW. The Publish card acts through AFFORDANCE OFFERS, not a bespoke port: `release.decide` needed its own offer-mint row (task-21209552) for exactly this reason, because the ladder's offer union in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts is a CLOSED type — adding a kind is a type edit plus a mint site, and a mint without the widening will not compile. Follow that precedent exactly: a LAZY FACT on the offer input supplied by the composition root, never a store walk from inside the ladder, resolved only for a goal that could actually hold an UNKNOWN publish (a per-poll walk over every goal is the 09-05 affordances hot-path incident repeating).

THE TARGET KEY IS A SAFETY PROPERTY. `readDurableLedger` keeps the last committed result per targetAggregateId, so a decision targeted at the bare goal id OVERWRITES the goal's durable record and drops it from `durableGoals` — the hazard affordance-planning-offers.ts already documents for preview and release. Target the resolve at the publish decision's own aggregate, never the goal id, and prove the goal survives a committed resolve.

THE CARD. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx gates Publish on `publish?.outcome !== \"UNKNOWN\"` (:91). For an UNKNOWN publish it shows the observation (delivered by the sibling observation row) and a resolve control offering NOT_TRANSMITTED and ABANDON, submitted through the offer exactly as the other cards submit theirs. The operator, not the daemon, asserts that the remote does not hold the sha, so the control must sit beside the observation it is deciding on. It is an OPERATOR affordance: `repository.publish_resolve` is human-only (row 3) and must never become staffable agent work.

ORDER. Depends on the service child (so the control never ships pointing at row 3's refusing stub) and on the observation child (so the card has something to show beside the control, and because both edit goal-publish.tsx).
definitionOfDone: The affordance read offers `repository.publish_resolve` for a goal whose latest publish is UNKNOWN, asserted BY VALUE on commandKind and targetAggregateId against the PRODUCTION surface read; the target is NOT the bare goal id, and an arm commits a resolve and asserts the goal is STILL present in the durable goal set with its state unchanged.

The offered-kind SET is asserted in both directions (set-equality, never `not.toContain`): offered for an UNKNOWN publish, absent for PENDING, PUSHED and REFUSED ones; and the kind is never staffable work.
The fact the ladder reads is a lazy fact supplied by the composition root, resolved only for a goal with a publish, following the release precedent.

The Publish card renders the resolve control only for an UNKNOWN publish, beside the observation, and submits NOT_TRANSMITTED or ABANDON through the offer; control-room arms assert the rendered control and the submitted payload by value, and that a refusal renders its code.

Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed` lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` for src/http/affordance*, and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (apps/control-room is in no other gate); `pnpm typecheck`.

THE PLAN'S PREMISE, MEASURED. The async handler never reads envelope.targetAggregateId or expectedVersion. decideAsync (daemon-command-decision-port.ts:75) commits nothing at the target. The resolve's only durable write is the receipt on publish:<goalId> (publish-ledger.ts:222). So a resolve sent through the real command edge CANNOT go red when the mint is retargeted, and after a real resolve stateOf(publish:<goalId>) necessarily becomes the receipt, as it does for every publisher receipt.
Step 4 will therefore carry TWO arms:
- (i) The release-precedent survival arm: a decision committed AT the offered target and version. This is the drill's subject; it proves both the goal's and the publish decision's durable records are unchanged.
- (ii) A real served-entry resolve. It proves the goal survives by value, the publish ledger still reads its request, and the resolve offer is withdrawn.

SCOPE GROWTH (+1 path): apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/publish-port.ts, the card's only wire. It gains `resolve` through spendOffer and reuses the module-private PUBLISH_LAYER, so no new *_LAYER is added and the boundary-roster and layer-visibility censuses stay unchanged.

SIZES: affordance-planning-offers.ts is 338 lines. affordance-read.ts is 661, already over the 400 cap and grown by many prior rows, so growth there stays at a few lines. goal-publish.tsx is 227.

NOTE: `pnpm typecheck` (`pnpm --recursive typecheck`) DOES typecheck control-room src/** including tests, so the CLAUDE.md claim otherwise is stale.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Filed by me today as a CHILD of task-21be6e90, delivering the operator-facing half of its DoD 2. dependsOn [task-a47babf8 (the service, so the control never ships pointing at row 3's refusing stub), task-52682237 (the observation, which this control sits beside, and which also edits goal-publish.tsx)]. Follows task-21209552's release.decide offer precedent exactly. Measured at HEAD 2026-09-18.

(1) THE CLOSED OFFER UNION. apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts:128-131 types the mintable kinds as `CompilerOfferKind | "approval.decide" | "approval.decide_intent" | "goal.cancel" | "goal.close" | "plan.propose" | "preview.decide" | "release.decide" | "repository.publish"`. Adding the kind is a type edit PLUS a mint site: a mint without the widening does not compile, and a widening without a mint offers nothing.

(2) THE LAZY-FACT PATTERN. `PlanningOfferInput` (:45) carries per-goal facts supplied by the composition root: `closeReadiness` (:52), `landedCommit` (:75), `previewReceipt` (:88). The resolve needs one more — for a goal, the decisionId of its UNKNOWN publish, or null — supplied by apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts and resolved ONLY for a goal that could hold a publish. A per-poll walk over every goal would repeat the 09-05 affordances hot-path incident.

(3) THE TARGET, AND THE SECOND HAZARD IT AVOIDS. `readDurableLedger` keeps the last committed result per targetAggregateId. Targeting the bare goal id overwrites the goal's durable record — the documented hazard. Targeting the PUBLISH decision's own aggregate (`publish:<goalId>`, minted at :241) would be the same hazard again: the resolve would overwrite the publish decision's durable result that the publish ledger reads. So the resolve targets a DISTINCT aggregate, `publish-resolve:<decisionId>`, keyed on the decision being resolved.

(4) HOW THE CARD FINDS ITS OFFER. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx:37-40 `publishOffer(frame, goalId)` matches `row["commandKind"] === "repository.publish" && row["targetAggregateId"] === `publish:${goalId}``. The control-room cannot import daemon code, so spelling the target on both sides of the package boundary is the ESTABLISHED pattern here. The resolve matcher uses the decisionId the card already has from `RunGoalPublish.decisionId`. Each spelling carries a comment naming the other, so a future change edits both.

(5) OFFERED, NEVER STAFFED. The ladder's `staffAll` makes offers staffable, but `resolvePlanningOffers` fills compiler steps only from COMPILER kinds. An operator kind that is in neither COMPILER_OFFER_KINDS nor COMPILER_SCHEMA_KINDS is therefore offered to the operator but never becomes agent work — exactly how release.decide stays an operator affordance. `repository.publish_resolve` is also human-only and MCP-excluded (row 3).
